description: Feature schema for the Q-SHIELD communication-channel anomaly Isolation Forest. One sample = one summarized observation WINDOW on a single channel (primary or LoRa), not a single packet.

packet_rate.description: Number of packets received on this channel during the window, divided by window_seconds.
packet_rate.typical_normal_range: ~5-15 (assumed synthetic baseline; replace with real Pi baseline stats)

inter_arrival_time.description: Mean time between consecutive packet arrivals within the window.

jitter.description: Standard deviation of inter-arrival times within the window.

packet_loss.description: Fraction of expected packets (by sequence number) not received during the window.

rejection_rate.description: Fraction of received packets rejected by the crypto layer during the window (failed decryption, failed ML-DSA signature, rejected/replayed nonce). Replay/tampering is primarily handled by the crypto layer itself, not this model - this feature just lets rejection spikes contribute as an anomaly signal.

retransmissions.description: Number of retransmitted packets observed during the window (ACK timeout / NACK triggered resend).

excluded_features.rssi: Not available from hardware yet. Add as a v2 schema once the Raspberry Pi/LoRa side provides real values - do not fabricate it.
excluded_features.snr: Same as rssi - LoRa-side signal quality metric, add in v2 once real hardware data exists.

input_format: A dict with exactly the 6 keys above (any key order - code reindexes to feature_order before scoring), or a pandas DataFrame/CSV with these columns for batch scoring.
notes: All 'typical_normal_range' values are ASSUMED placeholders from synthetic data generation (see ml/data/generate_synthetic_data.py). They must be replaced with statistics computed from real Raspberry Pi baseline captures before this model is trusted operationally.
Training uses only assumed-normal synthetic data (unsupervised). Synthetic attack data is used for evaluation only, never for training.
